subject: Path analysis estimate on panel time series data

messages.author: a495211f8f95b361
messages.subject: Path analysis estimate on panel time series data
parts:
Hello, 

I am new in lavaan. I am doing an economical analysis with a large dataset of countries' time series from 2000 to 2020 to estimate the effect of macroprudential policy on inequality. I expect many indirect effects. Is it possible to estimate direct/indirect/total effect via path analysis using sem (lavaan package)? How to input the fixed/random effects parameters? I really appreciate your help. Thank you!

messages.author: f1530326ce101401
messages.subject: Re: Path analysis estimate on panel time series data
parts: > I expect many indirect effects. Is it possible to estimate direct/indirect/total effect via path analysis using sem (lavaan package)?
Yes! The tutorial page from lavaan (https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/mediation.html) has some useful information.
> How to input the fixed/random effects parameters?

I assume you are interested in multilevel mediation? In that case, you can perform multilevel mediation using the MSEM framework (see https://doi.org/10.1037/a0020141 or perhaps https://doi.org/10.1080/00273171.2018.1527676, although the latter specifically looks at the 1-1-1 setting). If you would choose to work with MSEM using lavaan, then it is important to know that random slopes are currently not available in lavaan.

Hope this helps! (Perhaps someone with more experience in the field will also respond and give you more(/better) advice.)

Best wishes,

Jasper
